gloss: look of the sky; weather conditions

definitions.gloss: look of the sky; weather conditions; sky
definitions.explanation: The appearance of the sky as an indicator of the weather. Often implies uncertain or threatening weather. Also used figuratively for the 'atmosphere' or mood of a situation.

examples.japanese: {空模様|そらもよう}が{怪|あや}しい。
{空模様|そらもよう}を{見|み}て{傘|かさ}を{持|も}っていくことにした。
examples.english: I looked at the sky and decided to bring an umbrella.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}から{空模様|そらもよう}が{悪|わる}く、{午後|ごご}には{大雨|おおあめ}になった。
examples.english: The sky looked bad from morning, and by afternoon it was pouring.

notes:
Literally 'sky pattern' — the appearance of the sky as a weather indicator. Often carries a nuance of uncertainty or concern about whether the weather will turn bad.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空模様|そらもよう}が{怪|あや}しい — the sky looks threatening
- {空模様|そらもよう}が{悪|わる}い — the weather looks bad
- {空模様|そらもよう}を{見|み}る — to check the sky/weather
- {空模様|そらもよう}を{気|き}にする — to worry about the weather

USAGE:
Can be used metaphorically for the mood or atmosphere of a situation, e.g., {会議|かいぎ}の{空模様|そらもよう}が{怪|あや}しくなってきた (the atmosphere in the meeting is turning sour).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {天気|てんき} — weather (neutral, general)
- {天候|てんこう} — weather conditions (more formal)
- {模様|もよう} — pattern; appearance; state of affairs
